# Design Document ## Overview The blog-core feature adds a fully readable, subscribable blog at `/blog` to the static-first Next.js site. It introduces a new Velite `posts` collection (MDX with frontmatter), four server-rendered routes (`/blog`, `/blog/[slug]`, `/blog/tags/[tag]`, `/blog/categories/[category]`), a single content-query module (`src/lib/blog.ts`), a static RSS 2.0 feed at `/feed.xml`, sitemap extension, build-time Shiki syntax highlighting with dual-theme CSS, and a draft workflow keyed off the `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` environment variable scoped to Vercel preview deploys. The design is entirely additive to site-foundation and professional-profile. The existing `pages` and `profile` Velite collections, the `` renderer, the shadcn `Card` primitive, the site-wide CSP, and the `next-themes` setup are reused without modification (the `ThemeProvider` requires one symmetric-class config tweak). The only new client-side surface is zero — all blog routes are server-rendered, statically generated, and ship no incremental client JavaScript beyond the Next.js baseline. Three fixture posts (`fixture-draft`, `fixture-code`, `fixture-reading-time`) are committed as `draft: true` content and serve as the substrate for every Vitest and Playwright assertion in this spec. They are visible on preview deploys (CI Build 1) and provably absent from production builds (CI Build 2 smoke check). ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - **Markdown-driven content pipeline**: New `posts` collection follows the established Velite pattern from `pages` and `profile` — frontmatter-validated MDX, build-time compilation, zero runtime cost. Velite v0.3.1 (already installed) exposes `MarkdownOptions.remarkPlugins`/`rehypePlugins` and a top-level `markdown?` config key (verified in `node_modules/velite/dist/index.d.ts`), so the dual-pipeline emit (`body` via `s.mdx()` + `bodyHtml` via `s.markdown()`) for RSS uses framework APIs with no monkey-patching. - **Shiki build-time highlighting**: `rehype-pretty-code` (Shiki under the hood) registered in both the `mdx.rehypePlugins` and `markdown.rehypePlugins` arrays via a single shared constant. Zero client-side JS for syntax highlighting (per tech.md "minimize client-side JavaScript"). - **Static-first deployment**: Every new route declares `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` and (for dynamic segments) `export const dynamicParams = false`. The RSS route handler is `force-static`. All output is prebuilt; Vercel serves static files. - **CSP compatibility**: All blog routes render under the existing `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` policy. Shiki emits inline styles on code-block spans which fall under the existing `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`. No CSP changes required. The RSS XML response is not CSP-scoped (CSP applies to HTML). - **Performance target (Lighthouse 90+)**: Existing `@lhci/cli` setup extended — four new URLs added to `lighthouserc.js`. No per-page JS budget growth. - **Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)**: Existing Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` pattern from contact-form smoke test reused for two-theme axe pass on four representative blog routes. - **next-themes for theme persistence**: Existing `ThemeProvider` reused; the only change is wiring `value={{ light: 'light', dark: 'dark' }}` so both classes are written symmetrically (required by the Shiki dual-theme CSS cascade in Req 9.2). ### Project Structure (structure.md) - **Route files** land under `src/app/(site)/blog/` per the existing route group convention: `page.tsx` (index, replaces the existing placeholder), `[slug]/page.tsx`, `tags/[tag]/page.tsx`, `categories/[category]/page.tsx`. The RSS route lands at `src/app/feed.xml/route.ts` per Next.js route-handler conventions and the structure.md tree. - **Helpers** land in `src/lib/blog.ts` — the single content-query module for blog posts, per the decomposition cross-spec convention. No additions to `src/lib/content.ts` (reserved for shared utilities; blog-core is the only consumer of these helpers today, so premature extraction is avoided per structure.md "Code Size Guidelines" and the decomposition's YAGNI stance). - **Components** land under a new `src/components/blog/` directory: `post-card.tsx`, `prev-next-nav.tsx`, `tag-chip.tsx`, `draft-banner.tsx`. No barrel files. All named exports. Server components by default. - **Content** lands in `content/posts/` (new flat directory, matching the existing `pages/` flat pattern). Fixture posts live alongside future real posts; the `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` env var controls visibility, not file location. - **Tests**: Vitest unit tests colocate with helpers (`src/lib/blog.test.ts`); Playwright E2E tests live under `e2e/tests/` (`blog-axe.test.ts`, `blog-no-js.test.ts`, `blog-draft-visibility.test.ts`, `blog-shiki-theme.test.ts`). - **CI orchestration scripts** land in `scripts/` per the existing convention established by `run-e2e.mjs`: `verify-production-build.mjs` and `validate-feed.mjs`. - **Styles**: The Shiki theme CSS lives in `src/styles/globals.css` (additions, not a new file), grouped with other token-driven theme styling. No CSS Module required — these are document-level rules. - **Naming**: All new files use `kebab-case.{tsx,ts}`. Components use `PascalCase` named exports. Hooks (none added). Slugs (route segments) use `kebab-case` enforced via the schema regex (Req 4.6). ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage - **`` (`src/components/shared/mdx-content.tsx:10`)**: Reused verbatim to render post bodies on the individual post page. Same renderer the profile page uses. No changes. - **`` (`src/components/ui/card.tsx`)**: The shadcn primitive is the container for every blog list item (index, tag page, category page), per the decomposition cross-spec convention "All gallery cards … use the shadcn `Card` component". Layout *inside* the card is blog-specific (``); the container styling is uniform. - **`` (`src/components/layout/theme-provider.tsx`)**: One-line config change to write symmetric `.light` / `.dark` classes via `value={{ light: 'light', dark: 'dark' }}` — required by the Shiki dual-theme CSS cascade. No new provider, no new wrapper. - **`siteConfig` (`src/config/site.ts`)**: Source of truth for `siteConfig.url` — every absolute URL in RSS, sitemap, and OG metadata is composed via `new URL(path, siteConfig.url)`. No hard-coded `https://matthewfield.ca` literals anywhere. - **Velite `pages` collection pattern (`velite.config.ts:13-24`)**: The new `posts` schema follows the same `s.path()` + `.transform()` slug-stripping pattern (`data.slug.replace(/^posts\//, "")`). The empty-collection-safe behavior site-foundation verified for `pages` extends to `posts`. - **`rehype-slug` (`velite.config.ts:79`)**: Already registered. The shared rehype array includes it so heading anchors work in both `body` (MDX) and `bodyHtml` (markdown) outputs. - **CI/dev script pattern (`scripts/run-e2e.mjs`)**: New `verify-production-build.mjs` and `validate-feed.mjs` follow the same conventions — Node script, top-of-file shebang, sync `fs`/`process.exit(non-zero)` on failure. - **`@axe-core/playwright` from contact-form pattern**: The two-theme axe pass on four blog routes follows the exact pattern established by `contact-axe.test.ts`. ### Integration Points - **Velite content pipeline**: New `posts` collection registered alongside `pages` and `profile` in `defineConfig({ collections })`. Top-level `markdown` config added to `defineConfig` (currently absent) to govern the `s.markdown()` compile path used for `bodyHtml`. Shared `sharedRemarkPlugins` and `sharedRehypePlugins` constants defined at the top of `velite.config.ts` and referenced from both `mdx` and `markdown` config blocks. - **`#site/content` path alias**: New `posts` collection is exposed via the existing alias. Page components import `posts` indirectly via `src/lib/blog.ts` helpers — never directly, to enforce the single-chokepoint pattern that prevents draft leaks. - **`src/app/sitemap.ts`**: Extended to enumerate post URLs, tag pages, and category pages via `getPublishedPosts()`, `getAllTags()`, `getAllCategories()`. Existing static-routes list preserved. - **`next.config.ts` `headers()` callback**: Extended to emit `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` site-wide when `process.env.VERCEL_ENV === 'preview'` (Req 7.11a). The existing CSP route block is preserved unchanged. - **GitHub Actions CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)**: Extended to invoke `pnpm build` twice (Build 1 with `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` for Playwright runs; Build 2 with the env var unset, followed by `node scripts/verify-production-build.mjs`). The feed validation step runs after Build 1. - **`lighthouserc.js`**: Four URLs added — `/blog`, `/blog/fixture-code`, `/blog/tags/fixture`, `/blog/categories/fixture`. ## Architecture The implementation has five layered concerns, each handled by a distinct module surface: 1. **Content schema** (`velite.config.ts` extensions): Defines what a valid post looks like. Owns the regex validation, the kebab-slug enforcement for tags/categories, the reading-time transform, the `bodyHtml` emit for RSS, the raw-HTML rejection in post bodies, and the shared remark/rehype plugin arrays. 2. **Query layer** (`src/lib/blog.ts`): The single chokepoint between Velite-emitted content and every consumer. Owns draft filtering (`getPublishedPosts()`), slug lookup, neighbors computation, taxonomy enumeration, and the build-time env-var scoping guards. 3. **Presentation** (`src/app/(site)/blog/**` and `src/components/blog/**`): Server-rendered pages and shared sub-components. No client components introduced. 4. **Syndication** (`src/app/feed.xml/route.ts` and `src/app/sitemap.ts` extensions): Build-time-generated discoverable surfaces. Consumes the query layer. 5. **Verification** (`scripts/verify-production-build.mjs`, `scripts/validate-feed.mjs`, Vitest unit tests, Playwright E2E tests): The dual-build CI orchestration that guarantees drafts cannot leak and the feed is structurally valid. ### Modular Design Principles - **Single File Responsibility**: Each page route handles one URL pattern. Each helper in `src/lib/blog.ts` does one thing (filter, lookup, neighbors, etc.). Each fixture post exercises one set of assertions. - **Component Isolation**: ``, ``, ``, and `` are independent server components. They take typed props derived from `posts` collection entries and have no internal data fetching. - **Service Layer Separation**: Page components never import `#site/content.posts` directly; they go through `src/lib/blog.ts`. The query helpers are the only module that reaches into the Velite output, guaranteeing every consumer applies the same draft filter and sort key. - **Utility Modularity**: Formatters (`formatReadingTime`, `formatPostDate`) live next to the queries that produce them in `blog.ts`. Premature extraction to `src/lib/content.ts` is avoided per the decomposition's YAGNI stance — a second consumer must materialize before the formatters relocate. ```mermaid graph TD A["content/posts/*.mdx"] --> B["velite.config.ts
(posts collection)"] B -->|s.mdx body| C["#site/content
(typed JSON + compiled MDX code)"] B -->|s.markdown bodyHtml| C C --> D["src/lib/blog.ts
(getPublishedPosts, getPostBySlug,
getPostNeighbors, getAllTags,
getAllCategories, formatters)"] D --> E["src/app/(site)/blog/page.tsx
(index)"] D --> F["src/app/(site)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
(post detail)"] D --> G["src/app/(site)/blog/tags/[tag]/page.tsx"] D --> H["src/app/(site)/blog/categories/[category]/page.tsx"] D --> I["src/app/feed.xml/route.ts
(RSS)"] D --> J["src/app/sitemap.ts
(extension)"] F --> K["src/components/shared/mdx-content.tsx
(reused)"] E --> L["src/components/blog/post-card.tsx"] G --> L H --> L F --> M["src/components/blog/prev-next-nav.tsx"] F --> N["src/components/blog/draft-banner.tsx"] L --> O["src/components/ui/card.tsx
(reused shadcn)"] P["scripts/verify-production-build.mjs"] -.->|reads .next/| Q["CI Build 2 output"] R["scripts/validate-feed.mjs"] -.->|reads public/feed.xml| S["CI Build 1 output"] ``` ## Components and Interfaces ### Velite `posts` collection (`velite.config.ts`) - **Purpose:** Validates post frontmatter, emits both compiled MDX (`body`) and prerendered HTML (`bodyHtml`), computes `readingTime`, derives the slug, and rejects raw HTML in post bodies. - **Interfaces (public via `#site/content`):** - `posts: Post[]` — typed array of all parsed posts (drafts included; filtering is the query layer's job). - **Dependencies:** `velite`, `rehype-slug` (existing), `rehype-pretty-code` (new), `remark-gfm` (new), `remark-parse` + `unist-util-visit` + `mdast-util-to-string` (new — for the reading-time AST extractor and the raw-HTML rejection visitor), `reading-time` (new), `shiki` (new — peer dep of `rehype-pretty-code`). - **Reuses:** The same `s.path().transform()` slug-stripping pattern used for `pages` (`velite.config.ts:23`). - **Key implementation pins:** - **Shared plugin constants** declared once at the top of `velite.config.ts`: ```ts const sharedRemarkPlugins = [remarkGfm]; const sharedRehypePlugins = [rehypeSlug, [rehypePrettyCode, prettyCodeOptions], rehypeAbsolutizeUrls]; ``` Both arrays are passed to `mdx.remarkPlugins`/`mdx.rehypePlugins` AND `markdown.remarkPlugins`/`markdown.rehypePlugins`. Stateless-instance constraint per Req 11.7a: `rehypeAbsolutizeUrls` is a pure visitor with no per-file state (no `Set` of seen URLs, no closure-captured state) — verified by code review at implementation time. - **Reading-time transform** runs after frontmatter parsing inside the `posts` schema `.transform()` callback. Implementation: parse the raw markdown body with `remark-parse` + `remark-gfm` (same plugins as `sharedRemarkPlugins`), walk with `unist-util-visit` dropping `code` and `html` node types, recursing into `mdxJsxFlowElement`/`mdxJsxTextElement` children, then flatten with `mdast-util-to-string({ includeImageAlt: true })`. Pass the flattened string to `readingTime()` and clamp `minutes = Math.max(1, Math.round(result.minutes))`. The raw markdown body is available inside the transform via `meta.content` (Velite exposes the original file contents on `meta`). - **Raw-HTML rejection** (Req 3.7 / Req 1.12 enforcement): a second walk over the same mdast tree throws a named error if any `type: 'html'` node is encountered, with a message identifying the offending file and the leading character of the HTML snippet so the author can locate it. - **`bodyHtml` field** emitted via `s.markdown()`. Schema: `bodyHtml: s.markdown()`. The `markdown` top-level config in `defineConfig` sets the same shared plugins so the output mirrors the page-rendered HTML structure. - **`prettyCodeOptions`** pinned: `{ theme: { light: 'github-light', dark: 'github-dark' }, defaultColor: false, keepBackground: false }`. `defaultColor: false` is the variable-bridged emit mode (Req 9.2's "rehype-pretty-code emit format"); `keepBackground: false` lets the site's CSS supply the surrounding background per Req 9.5. - **`rehypeAbsolutizeUrls`** is a small (~40 LOC) hand-rolled HAST visitor: walks the tree, for every `element` with `tagName === 'a'` or `tagName === 'img'`, if `properties.href`/`properties.src` is relative or root-relative (starts with `/` but not `//`) it rewrites to `new URL(value, siteConfig.url).toString()`. Implementation lives in a sibling file `lib/rehype-absolutize-urls.mjs` imported by `velite.config.ts` (Velite config supports `.mjs` imports natively); placed outside `src/` to avoid importing `siteConfig.url` from `src/config/site.ts` inside the velite config — instead the visitor accepts the base URL as a factory parameter: `rehypeAbsolutizeUrls({ baseUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? siteConfig.url })`. `siteConfig.url` is the launch fallback to avoid making the env var build-required. - **`.strict()` mode**: applied to the posts schema (Velite forwards to zod's strict mode) — rejects unknown frontmatter keys. ### `src/lib/blog.ts` - **Purpose:** Single chokepoint for every blog-content query and formatter. Implements draft filtering, sort, neighbors, taxonomy, and the build-time env-var scoping guards. - **Interfaces (named exports):** ```ts export function getPublishedPosts(): Post[]; export function getPostBySlug(slug: string): Post | null; export function getPostNeighbors(slug: string): { previous: PostMeta | null; next: PostMeta | null }; export function getAllTags(): string[]; export function getAllCategories(): string[]; export function getPostsByTag(tag: string): Post[]; export function getPostsByCategory(category: string): Post[]; export function formatReadingTime(minutes: number): string; export function formatPostDate(iso: string): { datetime: string; display: string }; export type Post = (typeof posts)[number]; export type PostMeta = Pick; ``` - **Dependencies:** `#site/content` (`posts` array). - **Reuses:** Nothing from the existing site — this is a new module. Imports the typed `posts` collection from `#site/content`. - **Key implementation pins:** - `getPublishedPosts()` reads `process.env.BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` and `process.env.VERCEL_ENV` **inside the function body** (Req 7.5), not at module top-level. Bundler-inlining is not in play (these are not `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`), but call-time reads enable Vitest tests to mutate env state per-test. - **Build-time guards (Req 7.12)** fire inside `getPublishedPosts()` before the filter: `(a)` if `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS === '1'` AND `VERCEL_ENV === 'production'` throw; `(b)` if `VERCEL_ENV === 'preview'` AND `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS !== '1'` throw. Both messages name the variables and reference Req 7.3. - **Sort key** (one place, used everywhere): a private `byDateDescSlugAsc(a, b)` comparator. Compares `date` ISO strings lexicographically (correct because `s.isodate()` produces sortable strings), then `slug` lexicographically. The same comparator is used for the index, taxonomy pages, RSS, and the neighbors computation. - `getPostNeighbors(slug)` is pure (takes the sorted, draft-filtered array via `getPublishedPosts()` internally, but the helper signature consumed by the page is `(slug) => { previous, next }`). For unit testing, a private `_neighbors(posts, slug)` is exported under a `__testing` namespace OR the test mutates env state to control the post array — the chosen approach is a private export for testability without env mutation. - `getAllTags()` / `getAllCategories()`: enumerate non-draft posts, flatten the arrays, deduplicate, sort lexicographically. Empty array safe. - `formatReadingTime(minutes)`: `\`${minutes} min read\``. The minimum-1 clamp lives in the Velite transform (Req 6.1), so the formatter assumes `minutes >= 1`. - `formatPostDate(iso)`: returns `{ datetime: iso, display: new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { year: 'numeric', month: 'long', day: 'numeric' }).format(new Date(iso)) }`. Server-only (called from server components and the RSS route handler). ### `src/app/(site)/blog/page.tsx` (index) - **Purpose:** Reverse-chronological list of all non-draft posts; replaces the placeholder. - **Interfaces:** Default-exported React server component. `generateMetadata()` returns title, description, canonical, RSS alternate link, and (when `VERCEL_ENV === 'preview'`) `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` for defense-in-depth. - **Dependencies:** `getPublishedPosts`, ``. - **Reuses:** `` (indirectly via ``), site `` template from root layout. - **Key pins:** `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`. Removes the existing `robots: { index: false }` override at `src/app/(site)/blog/page.tsx:8`. Empty state renders "No posts yet — check back soon." inside the same container. `<title>` is `"Blog"`. `max-w-3xl` container. ### `src/app/(site)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (post detail) - **Purpose:** Renders a single post with header (title, dates, reading time, tags, draft banner), body (MDX via `<MDXContent />`), and footer (prev/next nav). - **Interfaces:** Default-exported async server component receiving `{ params: { slug: string } }`. `generateStaticParams()` returns `getPublishedPosts().map(p => ({ slug: p.slug }))`. `generateMetadata({ params })` returns the per-post metadata per Req 3.6 plus draft-aware `[DRAFT]` prefix and `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` for drafts. - **Dependencies:** `getPostBySlug`, `getPostNeighbors`, `formatPostDate`, `formatReadingTime`, `<MDXContent />`, `<PrevNextNav />`, `<TagChip />`, `<DraftBanner />`. - **Reuses:** `<MDXContent />` (shared, profile-page pattern), `@tailwindcss/typography` prose classes. - **Key pins:** `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`, `export const dynamicParams = false`. The prose container uses `prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert max-w-[75ch]`. `<DraftBanner />` renders conditionally on `post.draft === true` and lives inside the `<article>` body. Heading anchors come from `rehype-slug` already wired in the shared rehype array. Calling `getPostBySlug(slug)` and getting `null` triggers Next.js `notFound()` (covers the impossible-by-dynamicParams-false case as a defensive read). ### `src/app/(site)/blog/tags/[tag]/page.tsx` and `categories/[category]/page.tsx` - **Purpose:** Taxonomy filter pages — one post-list per tag/category. - **Interfaces:** Default-exported server components. `generateStaticParams()` returns `getAllTags().map(tag => ({ tag }))` (or categories). `generateMetadata({ params })` per Req 4.8. - **Dependencies:** `getPostsByTag` / `getPostsByCategory`, `getAllTags` / `getAllCategories`, `<PostCard />`. - **Reuses:** `<Card />` via `<PostCard />`. Same list layout as the index. - **Key pins:** `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`, `export const dynamicParams = false`. A "back to all posts" link to `/blog`. The two route files MAY share an internal `<TaxonomyList kind="tag" | "category" value={value} posts={posts} />` helper component co-located in `src/components/blog/taxonomy-list.tsx` to avoid duplication, but the route files remain independent per Req 4.2. ### `src/app/feed.xml/route.ts` (RSS 2.0) - **Purpose:** Static RSS 2.0 feed with full-content `<content:encoded>` for every non-draft post. - **Interfaces:** Exports `GET()` returning `new Response(xml, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/xml; charset=utf-8' } })`. Declares `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`. - **Dependencies:** `feed` npm package (new), `getPublishedPosts`, `siteConfig`. - **Reuses:** `siteConfig.url`, `siteConfig.description` for channel metadata; same fixed description string as the index page meta description. - **Key pins:** - Constructs a `new Feed({ ... })`, adds each post via `feed.addItem({ ... })` with `link`, `guid`, `description` (the lede), `content: post.bodyHtml` (with the CDATA-escape preapplied inside the Velite transform per Req 11.10), `date: new Date(post.date)`, and `categories: dedup([...post.tags, ...post.categories]).map(name => ({ name }))`. Calls `feed.rss2()` and returns the string. - The `]]>` → `]]]]><![CDATA[>` substitution happens **inside the Velite `bodyHtml` transform** (Req 11.10), not in the route handler — the feed package wraps the already-escaped string in CDATA without further escape. - The Velite-emitted `bodyHtml` already has absolutized URLs (Req 11.8) and Shiki-highlighted code (Req 11.9), so the route handler does no rewriting. ### `src/app/sitemap.ts` (extension) - **Purpose:** Extend the existing sitemap to enumerate posts, tag pages, and category pages. - **Interfaces:** Existing default export `sitemap()` updated to spread the new dynamic entries onto the existing static array. - **Dependencies:** `getPublishedPosts`, `getAllTags`, `getAllCategories`, `siteConfig`. - **Reuses:** The existing `siteConfig.url` composition pattern at `src/app/sitemap.ts:23`. - **Key pins:** Post `lastModified` = `new Date(post.updated ?? post.date)`. Tag/category `lastModified` = max `date` of any post in the taxonomy (computed once per build, no per-entry walk). ### `src/components/blog/post-card.tsx` - **Purpose:** Renders one post entry on the index and taxonomy pages. - **Interfaces:** `<PostCard post={post} />` — server component, takes a single `Post` prop. - **Dependencies:** `<Card />` (shadcn), `<TagChip />`, `formatPostDate`, `formatReadingTime`, Next.js `<Link>`. - **Reuses:** shadcn `Card`. No new card primitive. - **Key pins:** Wrapped in `<article aria-labelledby={titleId}>`. Title is a `<Link href={\`/blog/${post.slug}\`}>`. Reading time and date sit under the title; description is the lede; tag chips render under the description. ### `src/components/blog/prev-next-nav.tsx` - **Purpose:** Renders the prev/next footer on the post detail page. - **Interfaces:** `<PrevNextNav previous={prev} next={next} />` — server component. - **Dependencies:** Next.js `<Link>`. - **Reuses:** None. Pure presentation. - **Key pins:** Omits affordances entirely when null (no disabled links per Req 5.3). `aria-label` on each link includes `"Previous post: <title>"` / `"Next post: <title>"`. Returns `null` when both props are null (Req 5.4). ### `src/components/blog/tag-chip.tsx` - **Purpose:** Renders a single tag (or category) chip with a link to its taxonomy page. - **Interfaces:** `<TagChip kind="tag" | "category" value={value} />`. - **Dependencies:** Next.js `<Link>`. - **Reuses:** None. - **Key pins:** 44×44 px minimum touch target per Req 13.4 — Tailwind `min-h-11 min-w-11 inline-flex items-center px-3` or similar. ### `src/components/blog/draft-banner.tsx` - **Purpose:** Renders the visible "DRAFT — not yet published" banner inside the article body. - **Interfaces:** `<DraftBanner />` — server component, takes no props (renders only when included). - **Dependencies:** None. - **Reuses:** Token-driven `destructive` color treatment from `tokens.css`. - **Key pins:** Lives **inside the article DOM** so a screenshot of the article body is self-identifying as a preview (Req 7.7). ### `scripts/verify-production-build.mjs` - **Purpose:** Asserts the `fixture-draft` slug is absent from every output surface of CI Build 2 (production-mode build with drafts unset). - **Interfaces:** Node script invoked as `node scripts/verify-production-build.mjs` from CI. Exits 0 on pass, non-zero with a diagnostic message on any violation. - **Dependencies:** Node built-ins (`fs`, `path`). - **Reuses:** The shebang + sync-fs + `process.exit(non-zero)` pattern from `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`. - **Key pins:** Checks (Req 7.14): absence of `.next/server/app/blog/fixture-draft/` directory, absence of `/blog/fixture-draft` substring in `public/feed.xml` and the rendered sitemap, absence of the fixture-draft title/slug in `/blog/index.html`, every `/blog/tags/<tag>/index.html`, and every `/blog/categories/<category>/index.html`. Each violation is reported with a clear file + slug message before exiting. ### `scripts/validate-feed.mjs` - **Purpose:** Validates the generated `public/feed.xml` as well-formed XML containing the required RSS 2.0 elements. - **Interfaces:** Node script. Exits 0 on pass, non-zero with diagnostic on failure. - **Dependencies:** A lightweight XML parser (`fast-xml-parser` — small, no native deps; added to devDependencies). Full schema validation deferred per Req 11.12 — minimal structural check is the chosen approach. - **Reuses:** `scripts/run-e2e.mjs` pattern. - **Key pins:** Parse the XML; assert root is `<rss version="2.0">`; assert `<channel>` exists with `<title>`, `<link>`, `<description>`; assert at least one `<item>` when posts exist (skip the at-least-one check when fixtures are also expected to be absent — Build 1 always has them present, so the check is unconditional in practice). ### `src/styles/globals.css` (additions) - **Purpose:** Implements the Shiki dual-theme CSS cascade per Req 9.2 — explicit class wins over `prefers-color-scheme` fallback. - **Interfaces:** Document-level CSS rules. - **Reuses:** The existing `.dark` class pattern from the token mapping and the existing `next-themes` integration. - **Key pins:** ```css /* Shiki dual-theme cascade (Req 9.2): - explicit .light / .dark on <html> always wins (covers user toggle) - @media (prefers-color-scheme) fires only when neither class is set (covers no-JS / pre-hydration) */ html.light [data-rehype-pretty-code-fragment] code { color: var(--shiki-light); background-color: var(--shiki-light-bg); } html.dark [data-rehype-pretty-code-fragment] code { color: var(--shiki-dark); background-color: var(--shiki-dark-bg); } @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { html:not(.light):not(.dark) [data-rehype-pretty-code-fragment] code { color: var(--shiki-dark); background-color: var(--shiki-dark-bg); } } ``` Token names mirror what `rehype-pretty-code` emits with `defaultColor: false`. Exact selector confirmed during implementation via inspecting a rendered fixture-code page; if the plugin uses different attribute names (`data-line` vs `data-rehype-pretty-code-fragment`) the selectors update accordingly without changing the cascade structure. ### `next.config.ts` (extension) - **Purpose:** Add the preview-deploy site-wide `X-Robots-Tag` header (Req 7.11a). - **Interfaces:** Extends the existing `headers()` callback. - **Reuses:** The existing route-matched headers array pattern. - **Key pins:** Reads `process.env.VERCEL_ENV` at build time (Next.js evaluates `headers()` at build). When `=== 'preview'`, emits one additional route block matching `/(.*)` with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`. When `=== 'production'` or unset, the block is omitted (the existing CSP block is untouched in either case). ### Test fixtures (`content/posts/fixture-*.mdx`) - **Purpose:** Stable test substrate per the Fixture Roster. - **Interfaces:** MDX files with `draft: true` frontmatter, the slugs and tags/categories defined in the Roster. - **Reuses:** The same Velite schema as production posts — no special-case schema for fixtures. - **Key pins:** All three fixtures share the `fixture` tag and `fixture` category so the taxonomy axe tests have ≥1 entry. Slugs (`fixture-draft`, `fixture-code`, `fixture-reading-time`) are permanently reserved per Req 7.14. ## Data Models ### `Post` (Velite-emitted type) ``` Post: - title: string # required, 1–120 chars - description: string # required, 1–300 chars - date: string # ISO 8601 datetime, sortable lexicographically - tags: string[] # kebab-slug regex enforced, dedup'd - categories: string[] # kebab-slug regex enforced, dedup'd - updated?: string # optional ISO 8601 datetime - draft: boolean # default false - slug: string # derived (filename) or override (frontmatter) - series?: string # forward-compat (unused in blog-core) - seriesOrder?: number # forward-compat (unused in blog-core) - readingTime: number # computed, integer minutes, >= 1 - body: string # Velite s.mdx() output (JS module string) - bodyHtml: string # Velite s.markdown() output (HTML string, CDATA-safe, absolutized URLs) ``` ### `PostMeta` (derived projection for prev/next) ``` PostMeta: - slug: string - title: string ``` ### `FeedItem` (RSS-layer projection — assembled in the route handler, not persisted) ``` FeedItem: - title: string - link: string # absolute URL via siteConfig.url - guid: string # = link, isPermaLink="true" - description: string # = post.description (lede) - content: string # = post.bodyHtml (CDATA-wrapped by `feed` package) - date: Date # = new Date(post.date) - categories: { name: string }[] # = dedup([...post.tags, ...post.categories]).map(name => ({ name })) ``` ## Error Handling ### Error Scenarios 1. **Post frontmatter violates the schema** (missing required field, invalid datetime, oversize string, unknown key with `.strict()` in effect): - **Handling:** Velite throws a named error during `next build` (or `pnpm dev`) with the offending file path and field. No coercion, no default-fill, no silent skip (Req 1.6). - **User Impact:** The author sees a build failure with the file name and field. CI fails; nothing deploys. Local dev fails fast. 2. **Tag or category violates the kebab-slug regex** (e.g. `'DevOps'`, `'C++'`, `'foo bar'`): - **Handling:** Velite schema validation fails with the exact message specified in Req 4.6: `"[velite/posts] content/posts/<file>.mdx: invalid tag/category slug '<value>' — must match ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$ (e.g. 'devops-tooling')"`. - **User Impact:** Author rewrites to the kebab form. Build fails until corrected. 3. **Post body contains raw HTML element** (e.g. `<aside>`, `<details>`): - **Handling:** The mdast `type: 'html'` visitor inside the Velite transform throws a named error identifying the file and the leading characters of the HTML snippet (Req 3.7). - **User Impact:** Author rewrites to markdown-native equivalent. Build fails until corrected. 4. **Capitalized JSX tag reference in post body without an MDX component registry** (e.g. `<Callout>`): - **Handling:** Velite's MDX compile via `s.mdx()` fails with a `ReferenceError`-style message naming the undefined component. (No additional handling required — the MDX compiler's own error surfaces correctly per Req 1.6.) - **User Impact:** Author rewrites or waits for a future spec to introduce the registry. Build fails until corrected. 5. **`BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` set on Vercel production deploy** (env-var scoping mistake): - **Handling:** `getPublishedPosts()` throws the Req 7.12(a) named error during `generateStaticParams()` execution. CI Build 2 also independently fails via `verify-production-build.mjs`. - **User Impact:** Production deploy fails before content reaches users. Operator fixes Vercel env-var scoping and redeploys. 6. **`VERCEL_ENV=preview` without `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1`** (env-var scoping mistake, the symmetric case): - **Handling:** `getPublishedPosts()` throws the Req 7.12(b) named error. - **User Impact:** Preview deploy fails with a clear remediation message. Operator scopes the env var to Preview in Vercel UI and redeploys. 7. **Empty `content/posts/` directory** (launch state, before any post is authored): - **Handling:** Velite emits `posts: []`. All consumers handle the empty array: index page renders the empty-state message; taxonomy pages have nothing to enumerate (`generateStaticParams()` returns `[]`); RSS emits a valid empty `<channel>`; sitemap omits post URLs (Req 1.8, 2.9, 7.14, 11.13, 12). - **User Impact:** Site deploys cleanly with no posts. Visitors see "No posts yet — check back soon." on `/blog`. 8. **Post page render error at static generation** (rare — implementation bug, MDX compile-time issue not caught by frontmatter validation): - **Handling:** Next.js' default behavior fails the build on `generateStaticParams`-targeted pages that error during static generation (Req 3.9). No try/catch swallows the error. - **User Impact:** Build fails. Implementer investigates the stack trace. 9. **CDATA-collision in code block body** (post legitimately demonstrates XML with `]]>`): - **Handling:** The Velite `bodyHtml` transform's post-compile substitution (`]]>` → `]]]]><![CDATA[>`) runs before the string is emitted. The `feed` package wraps the already-safe string in CDATA. - **User Impact:** None — the substitution is invisible to readers and feed subscribers (the resulting CDATA-split is semantically equivalent in any conformant XML parser). 10. **Unknown language in fenced code block** (e.g. ` ```nonsense `): - **Handling:** `rehype-pretty-code`'s default fallback to plaintext rendering. No build failure (Req 9.4). - **User Impact:** Block renders as plaintext styled like a code block. Author may correct the language tag in a follow-up commit. ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Testing (Vitest, colocated) - **`src/lib/blog.test.ts`**: - `getPublishedPosts()` with `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` → drafts present; with the env var unset → drafts absent (Req 7.6). - `getPublishedPosts()` with `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` AND `VERCEL_ENV=production` → throws Req 7.12(a) error (regex-match the message). - `getPublishedPosts()` with `VERCEL_ENV=preview` AND `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS≠'1'` → throws Req 7.12(b) error. - `getPostNeighbors()` against a synthetic 5-post array (private `_neighbors` export): correct prev/next at the chronological middle; null prev at oldest; null next at newest; single-post → both null (Req 5.3, 5.4). - `getAllTags()` / `getAllCategories()`: deduplication, lexicographic sort, empty-array safety. - `formatReadingTime(5)` → `"5 min read"`. - `formatPostDate('2026-04-23T12:00:00Z')` → `{ datetime, display }` with `en-CA` "April 23, 2026"-style output. - **Reading-time tolerance** (Req 6.5): runs the Velite-computed `readingTime` for the `fixture-reading-time` post against `± max(20%, 1 minute)` of the hand-counted prose-only word count ÷ 238. Fixture pinned to ≥1000 words so the 20% bound dominates. - **Env-state mutation pattern**: Vitest tests use `beforeEach`/`afterEach` to set and reset `process.env.BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` and `process.env.VERCEL_ENV`. This works because `getPublishedPosts()` reads at call time (Req 7.5). ### Integration Testing (Vitest) - **RSS body parity** (Req 11.11): the test compiles the `fixture-code` post's `bodyHtml` via Velite, fetches the rendered HTML for `/blog/fixture-code` from the dev/build output, and asserts (a) `<pre><code>` elements present in both with matching Shiki token-class patterns; (b) every `<h2>`/`<h3>` has matching `id`s; (c) every relative `<a href>` / `<img src>` in the fixture appears absolutized in both; (d) inline `<code>` elements present in both. Exact-string equality is not required — the assertions are on element presence and structural equivalence per Req 11.11's enumerated categories. - **Feed structural validation** (`scripts/validate-feed.mjs`): invoked as a CI step after Build 1. Parses `public/feed.xml`, asserts `<rss version="2.0">`, `<channel>` with required children, `<item>` count > 0. ### End-to-End Testing (Playwright) - **`e2e/tests/blog-axe.test.ts`** (Req 13.2): four routes × two themes = 8 axe runs against CI Build 1 (preview-mode, drafts visible). Inverse run for `colorScheme: 'light'` + storage `'dark'` asserts dark rendering. - **CI integration**: `pnpm test:e2e` is invoked against Build 1's static output via the existing `scripts/run-e2e.mjs` pattern.
